metadata.text: The following Letters are addressed to the friends of vital and practical religion^ because the author is persuaded that the very essence of true piety is concerned in this controversy ; and that godly men are the only proper judges of divine truth, being the only humble, upright, and earnest inquirers after it.

metadata.source_book: The Works of the Rev. Andrew Fuller, in Eight Volumes — Vol. 2: The Calvinistic and Socinian Systems Examined and Compared
metadata.text: So far from thinking, with Dr, Priestley, that " an unbiassed temper of mind is attained in consequence of becoming more indifferent to religion in general, and to all the modes and doctrines of it ;" he is satis- fied that persons of that description have a most powerful bias against the truth.

metadata.source_book: The Works of the Rev. Andrew Fuller, in Eight Volumes — Vol. 2: The Calvinistic and Socinian Systems Examined and Compared
metadata.text: Though it were admitted, that false principles, <iccompanied with a bigoted attachment to them, are worse than none ; yet he cannot admit, that irreligious men are destitute of principles.

metadata.source_book: The Works of the Rev. Andrew Fuller, in Eight Volumes — Vol. 2: The Calvinistic and Socinian Systems Examined and Compared
metadata.text: He has no notion of human minds being unoccupied or indiflferent : he that is not a friend to religion in any mode, is an enemy to it in all modes ^ he is a libertine ; he doeth evil, and therefore, hateth the light.

metadata.source_book: The Works of the Rev. Andrew Fuller, in Eight Volumes — Vol. 2: The Calvinistic and Socinian Systems Examined and Compared
metadata.text: And shall we compliment such a charac- ter, by acknowledging Uim to be in " a favourable situation for dis- tinguishing between truth and falsehood ?"* God forbid!

metadata.source_book: The Works of the Rev. Andrew Fuller, in Eight Volumes — Vol. 2: The Calvinistic and Socinian Systems Examined and Compared
metadata.text: It is he that doeth his will, that shall know of his doctrine.

metadata.text: The hum- ble, the candid, the upright inquirers after truth, are the persons who are likely to find it ; and to them the author takes the liberty to appeal.

metadata.text: The principal occasion of these Letters was, the late union among Protestant Dissenters, in reference to civil affairs, having been the source of various misconception, and, as the writer ap- prehends, improved as a mean of disseminating Socinian principles.

metadata.text: They considered themselves as applying merely for a dy?7 right ; and that, in such an applica- tion, difference in theological sentiment had no more concern than it has in the union of a nation under one civil head or form oi government.

metadata.text: This union, however, has become an occasion of many reflec- tions.

metadata.source_book: The Works of the Rev. Andrew Fuller, in Eight Volumes — Vol. 2: The Calvinistic and Socinian Systems Examined and Compared
metadata.text: Serious men of the Established Church have expressed their surprise, that some Dissenters could unite with others, so op- posite in their religious principles ; and, had the union been of a religious nature, it must, indeed have been surprising.
